days.file: Valentin de Boulogne - Saint Paul Writing His Epistles - BF.1991.4 - Museum of Fine Arts.jpg
days.title: Saint Paul Writing His Epistles
days.alt: St. Paul, bearded and wrapped in a red cloak, bends over a table of books and papers, writing with a quill.
days.look: Look again at Paul, pen in hand. What would you tell God about your own weakness?
days.license: Artist died 1632; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.file: Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn - Return of the Prodigal Son - Google Art Project.jpg
days.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
days.alt: A young man in torn clothes kneels with his face pressed against his father, who bends over him and rests both hands on his back.
days.look: Look again at the father’s hands on his son’s back. Where would you be in this scene?
days.license: Artist died 1669; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.title: The Liberation of Saint Peter
days.alt: Behind prison bars, an angel in a blaze of light wakes St. Peter between sleeping guards; to the right, the angel leads Peter out past the soldiers.
days.look: Look again at the light breaking into the prison. What chain would you ask Christ to break?
days.license: Artist died 1520; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.file: Christ in the Wilderness - Ivan Kramskoy - Google Cultural Institute.jpg
days.title: Christ in the Desert
days.alt: Jesus sits alone on a rock in a stony desert at dawn, his hands clenched together, deep in thought.
days.look: Look again at His clenched hands. What would you say to Him about your own temptation?
days.license: Artist died 1887; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.file: Angelico - Conversion St. Augustine - Musée Thomas Henry - from Thebaid dismembered.jpg
days.title: The Conversion of Saint Augustine
days.alt: In a walled garden, St. Augustine sits under a tree with his head in his hands, while another man stands by a house nearby.
days.look: Look again at Augustine, head in his hands, moments before he read. What is your own “not yet”?
days.license: Artist died 1455; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.title: The Light of the World
days.alt: At night, Christ in a white robe and a crown of thorns, his head shining with light, knocks at an overgrown door.
days.look: Look again at Christ, shining in the dark, knocking at the door. Where do you need His light today?
days.license: Artist died 1910; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.file: Peter von Cornelius - Joseph gibt sich seinen Brüdern zu erkennen - Google Art Project.jpg
days.title: Joseph Reveals Himself to His Brothers
days.alt: Joseph, in a white robe, embraces his youngest brother while the other brothers kneel and weep around him.
days.look: Look again at Joseph embracing the brothers who wronged him. What good could fill the space your habit leaves?
days.license: Artist died 1867; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.title: Confession
days.alt: In a dim church, a priest in a confessional raises his hand toward a man who leans in close beside him.
days.look: Look again at the priest’s raised hand. What would you bring to Confession?
days.license: Artist died 1747; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)

days.file: Scheffer, Ary - Saint Augustin et Sainte Monique - 88.45 - Musée de la Vie romantique.jpg
days.title: Saint Augustine and Saint Monica
days.place: Musée de la Vie romantique, Paris
days.alt: St. Monica, in a white veil, and her son St. Augustine sit close together, hands joined, both looking up toward the sky.
days.look: Look again at mother and son, looking up together. Who has prayed for you?
days.license: Artist died 1858; faithful photo of a 2D work (Commons: public domain)
